name: Obadiah
bio: Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace — a man who, Scripture notes, "feared the LORD greatly." When Jezebel was killing off the LORD's prophets, Obadiah had secretly hidden a hundred of them in two caves, fifty at a time, and supplied them with food and water at his own risk (1 Kings 18:3-4). During a severe famine, Ahab sent Obadiah out across the land searching for grass to keep the royal horses and mules alive. On the road, Obadiah encountered Elijah, whom Ahab had been hunting for three years, and fell on his face before him. When Elijah told him to go announce that Elijah was here, Obadiah panicked, fearing Elijah would vanish by the Spirit of the LORD before he could bring Ahab, leaving Ahab to kill him for the false report — and reminded Elijah of his own faithful record protecting the LORD's prophets. Elijah swore he would present himself to Ahab that very day, and Obadiah went to tell the king, setting up Elijah's confrontation with Ahab and the contest on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:5-16).
